title: Timmy Rogers, Buck Washington and learning the stage
summary: Child star Timmy Rogers encouraged him; with Buck and Bubbles, Austin Powell and Jumpin' George he did a grueling Atlantic City summer of three shows a night.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: O.K., now, coming along a little further, I wanted to be more clear than I am now about Timmy Rogers. It was with him that you worked with Buck Washington, right?
Say a little more about that if you would.

Well, Timmy was on stage when he was a child, with a thing called "Me and My Shadow". He was a child star and his tradition on stage goes way back. But he liked me because he could see that I had, you know, some potential to be on stage also. And he encouraged me. He was a friend and I learned a lot from him. And of course when we got our act together we played. And, incidentally, Linton Garner came in, Erroll Garner's brother. But this particular thing...we had two girls and Austin Powell, who had the "Cats and Fiddles", he wrote "I Miss You So", in fact "I Miss You So" is on the back of "Lush Life" of Nat King Cole's. Yeah. And Jumpin' George, he used to be with Arnett Cobb. He was a show drummer...
What was his name, Jumpin' George...?

I think his name was Jumpin' George Jones, I think his last name is. Anyway, we had an act and that opened up a new world to me, of the stage and stage business. And that gave me a new dimension, you know what I mean, 'cause the stage is very serious...a lot of people think...and of course Timmy was a comedian, but he sang and people thought that... you know people on stage...but it's very serious and dedicated worker...it opened up a new world for me. But Timmy Rogers encouraged me and so did Buck and Bubbles. He was my roommate and my car-mate when we go on the road. And he taught me a lot too. And then, of course, Austin Powell, you know. They were all stage people, you know. Yeah. We went to Atlantic City and did a whole summer and that almost killed me, because I had never...I had to open the show blowin' and singin'. We did three shows a night, seven nights a week and then on Saturday nights they did the breakfast shows...went into Sundays which made seven days. Then they'd bring these people in that had these parties on Sunday after-
noons. So we end up some weeks doin' nine days. I'd never been through nothin' like that before. But that was show business. (laughter)
